bug_semantics: Scriban's recursive-descent parser treats nested array initializers as expressions. ParseArrayInitializer consumes '[' then calls ExpectAndParseExpression, which calls ParseExpression; ParseExpression on TokenType.OpenBracket calls ParseArrayInitializer again. Deeply nested input such as '{{ ' + new string('[', 5000) + '1' + new string(']', 5000) + ' }}' therefore grows C# call-stack frames without a terminating depth bound. The GHSA-wgh7-7m3c-fx25 6.6.0 mitigation (default ExpressionDepthLimit applied inside EnterExpression) did not wrap ParseArrayInitializer, and at 6.6.0 EnterExpression only logged once then continued parsing, so Template.Parse of untrusted nested arrays still raised an uncatchable StackOverflowException and killed the process (CWE-674).
flaw_origin: The unbounded ParseArrayInitializer -> ExpectAndParseExpression -> ParseExpression -> ParseArrayInitializer cycle was first written in the public-history root commit that introduced the Scriban parser (2016-01-25, Alexandre Mutel). Later trivia/token/move commits did not invent that recursion. ExpressionDepthLimit arrived years later for a different path and still omitted this function until 7.0.0.
